state.misconception_label: Thinks you can find missing values in a given table by treating the row as linear and adding on the difference between the first two values given.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: The equation \( f=3 r^{2}+3 \) is used to find values in the table below. What is the value covered by the star? \begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline\( r \) & \( 1 \) & \( 2 \) & \( 3 \) & \( 4 \) \\ \hline\( f \) & \( 6 \) & \( 15 \) & \( \color{gold}\bigstar \) & \\ \hline \end{tabular}. I got \( 24 \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why did you choose to add on the difference between the first two values in the table to find the missing value? Can you explain why that approach might not be valid in this situation?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I thought it would work because the numbers were getting bigger, so I figured it was just a pattern. But now I'm not sure if that’s right since the equation is more complicated. How do I actually use the equation to find the missing value?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you identify any similarities or patterns between the values of \( f \) and the corresponding values of \( r \) in the table? How might those patterns help you use the equation to find the missing value?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher effectively addresses the linear addition misconception and maintains high cognitive demand, but Turn 3's vague request to find 'patterns' doesn't provide appropriate scaffolding when the student has already asked how to use the equation, and while the student recognizes their approach was wrong, they don't demonstrate actually using the equation correctly.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking, never provides direct answers, and in Turn 1 effectively uses the student's flawed reasoning (pattern-based approach) to expose why it might not work, which are all hallmarks of the Socratic method.
